name: Census Bureau Building Permits Survey (BPS)
what_it_measures: New privately-owned housing units authorized by building permits, by number of units in structure. Roughly 9,000 permit-issuing jurisdictions respond to the monthly survey (per HUD's SOCDS); about 900+ counties reach 100% monthly reporting completeness, with full nationwide county coverage only guaranteed in the annual rollup. Aggregated to county/place/metro/state/national.
coverage: national (~9,000 permit-issuing jurisdictions report monthly; ~900+ counties have complete monthly reporting, full county coverage otherwise annual)
granularity: county, place (permit-issuing jurisdiction), CBSA, state, national
history_available: monthly data back to January 1997 per HUD's SOCDS mirror of this survey; Census's own site holds comparable depth
access_method: No confirmed REST API for county-level data in this run (the Census EITS timeseries API appears to cover only national/regional New Residential Construction (`eits/resconst`), not county-level permits). County-level access is via direct bulk download: Census's 'Current Data' page on census.gov/construction/bps serves recent months as Excel files; legacy ASCII/comma-delimited text files were discontinued after October 2019. HUD's SOCDS Building Permits Database (socds.huduser.gov/permits) offers a web query tool over the same underlying county data back to 1997.
license: US government work / public domain (standard Census Bureau data terms).
rate_limit: n/a (bulk file download / web query tool, not a rate-limited API)
fills_gap: A new-housing-supply growth signal that generalizes nationally. The project's existing supply-side signals (housing_database, rezonings in app/sources/development.py) are NYC-specific Socrata/Open Data feeds; this is the closest nationally-available analog (new permits as a leading indicator of future supply growth in a neighborhood/county).
caveats: No clean documented REST API confirmed for county-level granularity in this run — this would be a bulk-file adapter (like zillow_research.py's CSV fetch) rather than an API-key adapter, and needs a format check directly on census.gov/construction/bps's 'Current Data' page before implementation (Excel now, ASCII before Nov 2019).

County-level permit counts give at most borough-level (5-way) differentiation inside NYC, since each borough is its own county — coarser than the NTA geography the other pillars use; its main value is for the stated any-US-neighborhood generalization goal, where county is often the finest free unit available anyway.
Consider whether HUD's SOCDS mirror (a cleaner, purpose-built query tool over the same data) is actually the easier integration point than Census's own page.
recommendation_note: Real, free, nationally-generalizing supply signal with a long history, but the access mechanics (bulk Excel/ASCII, not a clean API) need to be nailed down before an add-data-source implementation, and it adds little differentiation for NYC's 5-county geography today. Recommended for the US-generalization roadmap, not as an urgent NYC-focused win.
